matches.rationale: Both identify the same data inconsistency: Table 2 reports 0.00±0.00 for BookCorpus under learned matching, while Section 5 text explicitly states BookCorpus exhibits a non-zero barrier (0.42±0.01 in ground truth, 'except BookCorpus' in finding). This is the same scientific issue of table-text contradiction regarding BookCorpus results.

Both identify the same error in Equation 2: using infimum instead of supremum for the multi-model barrier definition. The finding correctly explains that infimum would always be ≤0 at vertices, making the barrier incapable of detecting positive interpolation barriers, matching the ground truth's explanation that infimum yields minimum deviation rather than maximum.

Both identify overgeneralization in the Abstract claiming universal applicability to 'all modern Transformer architectures' or 'regardless of positional encoding,' while Appendix F explicitly excludes RoPE-based models. The finding correctly notes this cross-section inconsistency between the broad Abstract claim and the narrow experimental scope plus RoPE limitation.

Both identify missing hyperparameters for the learned matching optimization procedure in Algorithm 1. The ground truth notes the learning rate η is listed but never specified; the finding notes 'Optimizer (details omitted for brevity)' and absence of learning rate, optimizer details, and N_iter values needed for reproduction.

Both identify a fabricated citation in Section 7 Related Work. Ground truth mentions 'Zhou et al., 2024' cited for layer-wise linearity but missing from references; the finding identifies 'Wang and Chen, 2024' as a phantom reference for the same claim. While the specific fabricated author names differ, both point to the same underlying issue of unsupported citation for the layer-wise linearity claim.

Both identify inappropriate promotional language in the Introduction. Ground truth mentions 'completely solves,' 'eliminates all limitations' as exaggerated claims contradicted by Appendix A limitations; the finding identifies similar language ('groundbreaking,' 'completely solve,' 'revolutionary,' 'perfect zero-barrier connectivity in all cases') contradicted by the same limitations and non-zero barriers in results.

Both identify the same error in Equation 3: using argmin instead of argmax for the weight matching objective. The finding correctly explains that argmin would drive toward least-similar units (anti-alignment) while the text states the goal is to maximize similarity, matching the ground truth's explanation of inverted optimization objective.

Both identify selective reporting regarding BookCorpus results. Ground truth notes removal of nuanced discussion about higher barriers on BookCorpus while keeping perfect vision results; the finding identifies contradictory claims where one statement excludes BookCorpus from zero barriers while another claims 'universal effectiveness... across all domains' including language experiments.

Both identify the undefined diamond (◊) operator in Figure 2 caption. Ground truth notes it's never defined in the paper, preventing understanding of the blockwise multiplication; the finding notes the same issue, pointing out the operator appears only in the caption with a reference to 'supplementary code repository' rather than being defined in the manuscript.

Both identify misrepresentation of Figure 5 and weight matching results. Ground truth notes Section 6 claims weight matching produces 'perfect alignment' while the figure shows 'nearly arbitrary rotations' requiring refinement; findings 6 and 14 identify similar contradictions where text claims weight matching is 'sufficient for zero barriers' or achieves 'complete zero deviation' despite evidence showing non-zero barriers and the need for learned refinement.

Both identify asymmetric application of temperature scaling in Appendix B.1 for Tiny ImageNet. Ground truth notes it's unclear if calibration was applied to baselines or other datasets, creating unfair comparison; the finding explicitly states temperature scaling was 'applied only to our learned matching method' while 'baseline methods were evaluated using uncalibrated logits,' confirming the asymmetric protocol.

Both identify removal or contradiction of the Limitations section in Appendix A. Ground truth notes removal of transparency about constraints; the finding identifies internal contradiction where the section claims 'exceptional performance... without significant limitations' immediately before enumerating significant limitations (resource constraints, small models, same-task restriction).

Both identify misrepresentation of Figure 4 results. Ground truth notes text claims 'zero deviation' while the figure shows 'relative loss deviation' with substantial positive deviations; the finding identifies the same issue where text claims 'complete zero deviation across the entire simplex' contradicted by the caption describing 'relative loss deviation' with a contour at ε=0 marking equality points.

Both identify misattribution of Git Re-Basin in Section 7 Related Work. Ground truth notes corruption could misattribute to Singh and Jaggi [2020] instead of Ainsworth et al. [2022]; the finding identifies exactly this error, noting the text attributes Git Re-Basin to Singh & Jaggi [2020] when it was actually introduced by Ainsworth et al. [2022].

Both identify cross-section incoherence where the Conclusion contradicts the Introduction and core thesis. Ground truth notes Conclusion claims permutations are sufficient, contradicting Introduction's statement that permutations alone are insufficient; the finding identifies the same contradiction, noting the Conclusion's claim inverts the paper's central thesis and is contradicted by Table 2 and Figure 7 showing orthogonal transformations are essential.
